signals.summary: Coastal small-town and island living framed as the slow-life ideal: quiet harbours, seaside cottages and unhurried Mediterranean and northern-European shores.
signals.why_now: Elle India '7 Coastal Towns Perfect For A Slow Living Escape' (101h), a 'Slow Living In The French Riviera' feature (70h) and Euronews 'Germany's small islands: nature and slow living' (246h). Object-and-place led and highly producible.

signals.summary: The 'morning routine' genre shifting toward evidence-led calm — morning light, movement and anti-inflammatory habits — as an aspirational slow-living centrepiece (setting the named-celebrity routines aside).
signals.why_now: Stylist 'The morning routine scientists swear by for better mood' (97h), EatingWell '5 Anti-Inflammatory Morning Habits' (102h) and a WSBT piece on a coffee brewer rethinking how you start the day (117h). Producible through light, coffee and objects without any face on camera.

signals.topic: Analog hours & the calm digital detox
signals.summary: The screen-time backlash maturing from 'digital detox' into named daily practices — 'NPC hours', 'landline mode' — represented by unplugged, analog domestic scenes rather than the phones themselves.
signals.why_now: Fresh this cycle: a first-person 'NPC hours beat cheat days for cutting screen time' piece (1.9h), CBS News on a family's digital-detox after-effects (12h) and Kids News on Australian students ditching devices (20h). Broad and current; producibility is only moderate since the subject is a behaviour, best shown through calm analog still-lifes.
